questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place where I could gain a lot of new experiences

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information is readily available, yet it is very self-reliant. Normally at UCPH, if you ask for further information or guidance, they will help out quite a lot in my experience. At Yonsei University, and South Korea in general, my experience was that this wasn't the case to the same extent. Nonetheless, everything worked out without too many problems.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university regularly sends out emails with all the relevant information you need. This makes it easier to know what you need to do. There was also scheduled an introduction day, where we were informed of all we needed to know. Furthermore, one of the universities biggest clubs provides mentors to a group of students. You get your mentor and group early on. This is a great way to mingle with students from all around the world, as well as you being able to consult your mentor regarding any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is relatively easy and you can always find something relatively quickly, unlike in Copenhagen. Seoul is big and has an excellent metro system. Everywhere there are 'goshiwon', which are cheap single-room accommodations. Students often use these due to their low cost. You can find them by searching on Google, or using Naver or Kakao maps and searching for 고시원.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
With goshiwons, depending on the place, it has fewer rules to follow but might not have as good facilities. Yet even then, no drinking alcohol and no guests in the room are be common rules in some goshiwons as well. They tend to be quite fair with the prices in my experience.
When I first arrived I had an Airbnb, which was a mistake, as it dirty, moldy and much more expensive. I would recommend other solutions than Airbnb.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Yonsei only has a certain amount of rooms for students. Even if one should wish to get housing on campus, this isn't necessarily possible.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Registration is very different from UCPH and a bit more difficult. Basically, it is a 3-level system based partly on bidding. At the first level, you get a certain amount of points and bid for courses. Whether you get the course depends on certain factors such as: is it related to your major? Are you a foreign student (national students get spots first)? How much did you bid on the course?
At the second level and third level it's a first come first served basis reg. the courses that still have spots left after the first level. The system is therefore quite competitive.

One should also notice, that there arent' that many courses for exchange student. Yet this also depends on what one's major is.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not much help. You have to follow the academic guideline provided. When I tried to reach out for help, they were not optimal at providing the information I needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I did not get all my first priority classes, but was very happy with the ones I ended up with.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Watch a youtube guide and make sure to read the academic guideline properly before starting registration. Perhaps download past year's guidelines in advance. You might not get all the courses you want, yet ultimately, everything should work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level depends on which course it is, yet generally, it is more or less the same level as UCPH. The format is very different, as one is graded not only on exams but on different factors as well, such as attendance, class participation, presentations, etc.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Depends on which course it is. The different professors had very different teaching styles. Some classes had more lecturing, others had more group discussion,s and so on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Theories of International Relations
The Rhetoric of Dreams
Anthropology of North & South Korea

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Theories of International Relations - if you want to get a better understanding of contemporary theories of international relations, as well as getting better at making and presenting your material.
The Rhetoric of Dreams - if you want something that is very creative and unconventional
Anthropology of North & South Korea - If you want to learn more about North Korea

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Seoul is generally a tad bit cheaper than Denmark. You can easily get a good meal for 50 kr. A large Big Mac meal is currently 38 kr. 
Nothing was really more expensive than expected, except certain types of food, like pizza.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are tons of clubs that one can join. Almost all exchange students join the mentors club, which is good for socializing, especially if you get a very social mentor.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I only joined the mentors club

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the other cities of the country and experience different places outside Seoul. Japan is close by too, so you can visit at a fairly cheap price.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The language barrier is the main problem and you can also tell that foreigners typically make their own groups. So there is a kind of parallel society within the country.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join clubs, speak with the Korean students in your classes (if there are any), make friends with other foreign students who have been here for longer. Go out to establishments where local students frequently visit.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing too major, yet there are some minor differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I appreciate how social people are here. They love to go out and eat and drink together. The city is lively every day, with people going out and having fun together.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to find some friends and to socialize early on
Make sure not to focus excessively on your studies
Don't be nervous about anything, you'll have a great experience

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of foreigners have problems with their credit cards sometimes not working here

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All of it. Difficult to pinpoint.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Course registration. Besides that, everything was quite easy.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
